newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan harvest pushed far behind by weather.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan harvest pushed far behind by weather.

text.p: Wet weather in the week ended October 7 pushed Saskatchewan harvest progress far behind both last year's pace and its five-year average, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its weekly update.
Bleaching and sprouting after recent killing frosts were widespread and wheat quality ratings fell further, it said.
For all crops, harvest was 55 percent complete versus 95 percent a year ago and 87 percent on average.
Spring wheat harvested 50 pct vs 98 pct last year and 87 pct average.
Durum harvested 57 pct vs 98 pct y/a, 98 avge.
Barley harvested 63 pct vs 99 y/a, 92 avge.
Canola harvested 64 pct vs 96 y/a, 85 avge.
Flax harvested 9 pct vs 77 y/a, 62 avge.
Sunflowers harvested 1 pct vs 11 y/a, 21 avge.
Peas harvested 84 pct vs 99 y/a, 90 avge.

"The heavy snowfall in the southern grain belt last week caused many standing crops to be flattened. Quality loss is expected to continue due to the wetness and frost," the provincial department said in its report.
"In many parts of the province, swaths are becoming prime feeding grounds for migrating ducks and geese," it added.

It said spring wheat quality ratings declined slightly in the week, with 74 percent of the crop now expected to grade out to No 1 Canada Western (CW), 18 percent to 2CW, seven percent to 3CW, and one percent to Canada Feed Wheat.
